Part 1 of a series on how to build an low cost cnc: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3vgjJikt9B4

Openbuilds.com is a great place to find free plans and the cheapest aluminum extrusions. The extrusions serve as the frame and base of the cnc. To drive the cost of the machine down you can cut and weld scrap steel instead of using manufactured extrusions. Ive seen this work just as well as the machines that cost 20k. From there you just have to understand that on a basic cnc there are three axes. The axes will give you the ability to create most shapes. 3 axes means you will be able to create 2.5 dimensional shapes. The more axes you add, the more complex your shape can be and the less work you ultimately have to do in getting that shape. You can make anything from a spoon to a car transmission. Your axes ultimately serve to move your milling head. The milling head is where you mount your mill. To drive the head around the platform and create the shape you desire out of raw material you need motors for your x and y axis. Nema stepper motors are the standard. The are pretty cheap. They wire up to drivers that are also pretty cheap. Then you wire your drivers to a controller such as a cheap arduino then hook that up to your good old pc. The nema motors turn a lead screw that is connected to a bearing which slides the frame for your milling head on a glide track. This enables the milling head to travel anywhere on an x,y axis on your platform. Software needed is mentioned in the youtube vids. Then you obviously need your milling head to travel up and down as well as all over your platform on a z axis. Just plop one more nema motor, lead screw and glide track in a vertical orientation. Your milling head will be on the end of your z axis. Learn this concept before you increase your amount of axes. But once you know this, you are golden.
